Analytics boards

Dashboards ("boards") of chart panels that put many probe series or metrics-store series on one canvas over 1 hour to 90 days — built-in boards per ADOM plus your own, with MetricsQL selectors that scale to the whole fleet.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereMonitoring → Analytics (every ADOM) (URL /monitoring/analytics/)

What is it?#

Analytics shows boards: named sets of chart panels. Each panel draws many series at once — every device's CPU, the ten busiest services, all collectors that are failing — so you can compare devices and periods. It is a renderer only: it reads stored probe samples/roll-ups and the local metrics store, and opening a board contacts no appliance.

What does it do?#

  • Shows the boards available in the current ADOM as tabs; built-in boards carry a lock icon (Built in — duplicate it to edit).
  • Draws each panel over the board's range: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, or a custom start/end (Apply).
  • Auto refresh: Manual refresh, Every 30 s, Every minute, Every 5 min.
  • Lets authorised users create, edit and duplicate boards, add/edit/delete panels and drag panels to reorder them.
  • Collection cadence (header button) lists every probe's declared and effective interval.
  • Boards with variables (Device, Service) show pickers whose values come from the metrics store.

Built-in boards#

Board Where visible Source
Fleet metrics (store) — CPU, memory, collectors failing every ADOM metrics store
Device drill-down — pick a Device: CPU, memory, sessions, conn/s, interfaces down, published services, collectors failing every ADOM metrics store
Service drill-down — pick a Device then a Service: up, sessions, conn/s, client/server RTT, app response (RTT and app response are per-policy FortiWeb readings; FortiADC reports them only per device, as satom_adc_*) every ADOM metrics store
Fleet overview — CPU, memory, availability heatmap, peak stats every ADOM probes
Traffic & policies (store) — device throughput, busiest policies, policies down FortiWeb ADOM metrics store
Traffic & sessions — throughput, sessions, HTTP transactions FortiWeb ADOM probes
Service health — response time, proxyd memory, interface drift FortiWeb ADOM probes
Entitlement & tokens — licence and token consumption, HA peer FortiAuthenticator ADOM metrics store
Identity health — licence and token probes with thresholds FortiAuthenticator ADOM probes

Boards created in the Global ADOM are visible in every ADOM; boards created in a product ADOM are visible only there (and not in Global).

Requirements#

  • Probe panels need probes (see Probes) and the deep_monitor sweep.
  • Store panels need the metrics store up and scrape targets running (see Metrics collection).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Viewing boards: the legacy view gate — any read permission, for example monitoring.view; all system profiles have it.
  • Creating, editing, duplicating and deleting boards, adding/editing/deleting panels, reordering: the legacy config_write gate (e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply). Without it the editing controls are not rendered and the endpoints return 403.
  • Built-in boards cannot be edited or deleted by anyone; the server refuses with Built-in boards are reconciled from code and cannot be edited. Duplicate it first.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: viewing analytics boards now requires a read permission instead of sign-in alone; Create board opens the new board, and custom boards have an Edit board form.

How to use#

Read a board#

  1. Open Monitoring → Analytics and click a board tab.
  2. Pick a range or enter a custom start/end and click Apply.
  3. On drill-down boards, choose the Device (and Service) in the pickers.

Make your own board#

  1. In the New board box at the bottom, enter a title, optionally a Description and Default range, and click Create board. The page opens on the new, empty board.
  2. Or open any board and click the duplicate icon (Duplicate this board) to get an editable copy named <title> (copy).

Edit a board#

  1. Open one of your own boards (built-in boards cannot be edited — duplicate them first).
  2. Expand Edit board under the board's header.
  3. Change Title, Description, Default range or Auto refresh (Manual refresh, Every 30 s, Every minute, Every 5 min) and click Save. The page reloads on the board.

Add a panel#

  1. On an editable board click Add panel.
  2. Fill Title, Visualisation, optional Subtitle.
  3. Under Series selection choose: - Rule — everything matching: a Metric (probe kind), optional Name contains and Devices (none = all in this ADOM). Keeps working as probes are recreated. - Explicit — these probes: tick Probes (up to 40). - Store selector — MetricsQL: a MetricsQL expression, optional Legend label (a label key such as device) and Unit.
  4. Set Value shown, Width, Height (px), Range override (Follow the board or a fixed range) and the options Min/max band, Secondary metric, Threshold lines, Compare with previous period.
  5. Click Save panel.

Drag a panel to reorder it; use the panel's edit and delete controls to change or remove it.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Visualisation line, area, bar, stat, gauge, heatmap, table, status Yes line
Series selection Rule, Explicit probes, or MetricsQL Yes MetricsQL
MetricsQL expression Validated by running it against the store before saving; up to 500 characters For MetricsQL topk(10, satom_policy_conn_per_sec)
Value shown For stat/gauge: last, avg, min, max, sum, healthy_pct No max
Width Quarter, Third, Half, Two thirds, Full width No Half
Height (px) 160–900 No 260
Range override Empty follows the board No 7d

Series names for MetricsQL are listed in Metric series reference.

Example#

🧪Example — Compare CPU of all FortiWebs over a month

  1. Create a board Monthly capacity review with default range 30d.
  2. Add panel → Title CPU, all FortiWebs → Visualisation line → Store selector — MetricsQL → satom_box_cpu_pct{kind="fortiweb"} → Legend label device → Unit %.
  3. Save panel. One line per device appears.

Result#

  • Board and panel changes write audit entries (analytics.board.create, analytics.board.update, analytics.board.duplicate, analytics.board.delete, analytics.panel.create, analytics.panel.update, analytics.panel.delete).
  • Nothing on the appliances changes.

Troubleshooting#

"The store rejected that expression: …"#

The metrics store could not execute the expression. Fix the syntax or the series name. The message includes the store's error.

"A store panel needs a MetricsQL expression." / "Select at least one probe." / "A rule needs a metric or at least one device."#

Fill the field required by the chosen Series selection.

A panel shows an error instead of a chart#

A failed query is drawn as an error, never as an empty chart. Check the store on Collection, or that the board's variables are selected.

A chart has gaps#

Gaps are periods without samples (device down, sweep not running, collector failing). SATOM never draws a line across missing data.

"No boards are available in this ADOM yet."#

No built-in board applies and nobody created one here. Create one with New board (needs config_write).

Collection cadence shows 0#

No deep_monitor sweep is scheduled, so no probe is actually collected. See Scheduled actions.

"Edit board" is missing#

The board is built in (lock icon) or you lack config_write. Duplicate a built-in board to get an editable copy.

Advanced#

Advanced Resolution and data sources
  • Probe panels read raw samples, hourly roll-ups (90 days) or daily roll-ups (2 years); a panel uses one resolution for all its series and the footer states which.
  • Store panels choose a query step that keeps about 600 points per series and print the step.
  • Built-in boards are reconciled from the code at every start-up, so a release can improve them; your own boards are never touched. If one of your boards already holds a built-in board's internal name (slug), the built-in is left alone rather than overwriting it.
  • The Create board and Edit board forms redirect back to the board; scripts that post to the same endpoints without the form's redirect flag still receive JSON ({"ok": true, "board": …}).
